chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Salih, from Abdullah ibn Abbas.

Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'When he recovered, he said: Glory be to You! I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers.' He said: It means: Glory be to You, I repent to You for asking to see You, and I am the first of the believers that You cannot be seen.

key_terms.رؤية: Ru'ya - vision/sight, here referring to seeing God
key_terms.سبحانك: Subhanaka - Glory be to You, declaring God's transcendence

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas say about the meaning of Quran 7:143 and Moses asking to see God?
ai.summary: This hadith provides Ibn Abbas's exegesis of Quran 7:143, which describes Moses recovering after asking to see God and the mountain crumbling. According to Ibn Abbas, Moses's repentance was specifically for requesting to see God, and his declaration of being 'the first of the believers' meant he was the first to affirm the impossibility of seeing God. This interpretation supports the theological position that God is beyond physical vision, a view central to many Islamic theological schools.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi from his father Muhammad b. Khalid from Ahmad b. al-Nadr from Muhammad b. Marwan from Muhammad b. al-Sa’ib from Abi Salih from `Abdullah b. `Abbas.

Regarding His saying, “When he recovered, he cried, ‘Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance and I am the first of the believers’” [7:143] he said: Glory be to You, I repent to You for asking to see You. I am the first of the believers that You cannot be seen.
